precepts.text: Do what? Flee also youthful lust. The Bible says, "Flee also youthful lusts, but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart." Go back to 3 and 6. Now.
precepts.point: For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women. Silly women, laden with sins. Stop. What scripture will we go back to for that? Read it again. I forgot. Go back. Go back. Go back. Verse 22. Go back. Come on, y'all. Stay with me, y'all. The topic has not changed. Come on. Verse 22 of chapter 2.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

precepts.why:
“For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.” To understand who these are, go back to chapter 2, verse 22, because this is one long letter and the topic has not changed: “Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.”

The men of the last days are “lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy”, without natural affection toward their brothers and sisters, trucebreakers, false accusers. Incontinent means you are all over the place: no guideline, no law, no discipline. Fierce means angry. Traitors, heady, high-minded, “lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.”

“Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof.” Who is that? Israel, and more specifically the vessels of dishonour, the wood and the earth. You have a form of godliness, but you deny the laws of God; you follow no law. “from such turn away.” Not entertain them: turn away. God says turn away from those brothers that are dishonourable, the wood and the earth, and leave them the hell alone. In meekness you instruct those that oppose themselves, that “they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will”, but you do not walk with them.

These are the men who did not flee youthful lusts. They creep into houses and lead captive silly women: you get a silly woman who just came into the body and doesn’t know a damn thing, you crop yourself next to her and say you are her counselor now, I’m going to counsel you, sister, I got you. And she is laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.

So flee youthful lusts, and follow righteousness, faith, charity and peace with those that call on the Lord out of a pure heart. That is what separates the gold and silver from the wood and the earth. The precious sons of Zion are “comparable to fine gold”, and God said it, not man; but youthful lusts have turned the gold dim and made us earthen pitchers.

precepts.text: This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof. You know why it says a form of godliness? That is the fringes and the border of blue, walking around with your Bible saying all the greetings, but you are really not keeping the commandments in your heart. From such turn away: the same thing he said in the chapter before, purge yourself from these.
precepts.point: If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work. When you purge a plant you are pruning it, taking away the bad elements. Likewise with us: the bad elements among us, you have to cut off. I knew which brothers I always used to get in trouble with; I had to cut them off and hang out with leadership.
precepts.why:
Paul says in a great house there are vessels “of gold and of silver” and also “of wood and of earth”, and “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour.” The next chapter names who those vessels of dishonour are: “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.”

“Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof.” Why does it say a form of godliness? That is the fringes everybody wears and the border of blue, walking around with your Bible, saying Most High, in Christ, blessed heartily. But you are not keeping the laws in your heart. You are really not keeping the commandments.

The great house is the nation of Israel, the real nation of Israel. There are brothers and sisters of gold and silver, applying what we read in 1 Peter 2:1-2. And there are brothers and sisters with fringes and a border of blue who are no damn good. They have not changed their lives; they are the same as they were two, three years ago. Not the new people who just came in, but people who have been with us for years and are still grimy: still that secret adulterer, that liar, complainer, murmurer. You are that wood and that earth. In every IUIC school there are men and women of honour and of dishonour, and the captains must be able to identify which is which. If you can’t do that, there is a problem.

“from such turn away.” That is what he said in the chapter before: purge yourself from these. Purge means cut them off, cut them loose. When you purge a plant you are pruning it, taking away the bad elements. Likewise with us: the bad elements among us, you have to cut off. You know which brothers always get you in trouble. Rolling with grimy brothers, you can almost get arrested many a time; cut them off, say I’m not rolling with y’all no more, and hang out with leadership. That is how you become a vessel “sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.”

precepts.text: In a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour. If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use. The bank is his great house; your work, your love, your zeal, your understanding, bring it into the bank, the congregation.
precepts.point: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me. Churches don't read that; churches will look at that and go, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. You know what it means further? You ain't going to just be able to do what you want to do. You was put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, then there's no reason for you to live. He said, if you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?” This is the bank: the congregation. Usury means interest. So when Christ comes back, he wants interest on what he gave each of us.

Paul shows the great house: “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The bank is his great house. Your work, your love, your zeal, your understanding: bring it into the bank, the congregation.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” The servant who brings what he was given into the house and purges himself becomes a vessel of honour, fit for the master's use when he returns and requires his own with usury.

precepts.text: For our conversation is in heaven, from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ. We can't be entangled with the affairs of this life. What does God want us to do? What does God require of us? What is God's mission? Gather the twelve tribes of Israel from the four corners of the earth. Let the elect be sealed; let the 144 be sealed, so we can go home.
precepts.point: That he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier: in order for us to please God, who have called us to be a soldier, we cannot be entangled with the affairs of this life. If you entangled with the affairs of this life, that means you want to please men. We can't move like that. We got to be good soldiers with the mind of a judge, which comes from that biblical education.
precepts.why:
If Christ is our commander, what does that make us? Soldiers. “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” And a soldier cannot live for this world: “For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.”

We are at war. Spiritual war. We don’t use guns or weapons or any of that stuff, but we are at spiritual war, and spiritual war is the most powerful mode of warfare. Our forefathers understood that in this gospel, this mission we are on, we are all soldiers on the battlefield. That is how Paul referred to his fellow laborers.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” In order to please God, who has called us to be soldiers, we cannot be entangled with the affairs of this life. If you are entangled with the affairs of this life, that means you want to please men. We can’t move like that. Our conversation is in heaven, and we are looking for the Saviour to come from there.

So what does God want us to do? What does God require of us? What is God’s mission? Gather the twelve tribes of Israel from the four corners of the earth. Let the elect be sealed; let the 144 be sealed, so we can go home. That is the business of a good soldier of Jesus Christ, with the mind of a judge that comes from biblical education, instead of the affairs of this life.

precepts.text: But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth. The great house is the nation of Israel, the twelve tribes. In every school there are men and women who are gold and silver, and it is up to you to discern who they are; and in every school there are also brothers and sisters of wood and of earth. This is not about new brothers and sisters who just walked through the door: it is about men and women in this truth for years who have not changed, still murmurers and gossipers, no work, no effort to study, treating this like a social club, a place to hang out. If a man therefore purge himself from these: you have to know your circle. When the Bishop came into the truth he had a circle of brothers he was always in trouble around, and he had to change his circle and get around leadership and the elders to get his mind right. Do not worry about hurting feelings: if you know they are not right, separate from them. Then shall you be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use: then can God use you, send you to a city and you could grow a whole congregation. Like Isaiah said to the Lord: send me. And this is also why we cannot join with other camps that practice what God condemns: it is based on what we just read.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness. And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together: wicked Israel gets the same judgment as Esau. They shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired: the idols. Confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen: the churches. As an oak whose leaf fadeth: your understanding is gone. As a garden that hath no water: no water of understanding. And they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them: God gets rid of what he cannot use.
precepts.why:
God will “purely purge away thy dross.” Paul uses that same word, purge. “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver.” The great house is the nation of Israel, the twelve tribes. We are not speaking for the other camps, with their cookouts on the Sabbath, their raping of girls, their stealing money for Maseratis and beating the baby mothers; we speak for Israel United in Christ. In every IUIC school, Philly, DC, Virginia, New York, Atlanta, Connecticut, OKC, there are men and women who are gold and silver, and it is up to you to discern and identify who they are.

“but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” In every school there are also brothers and sisters of wood and of earth: they are not right. This is not about new brothers and sisters who just walked through the door; we all walk in not right. It is about men and women in this truth for years who have not changed: still murmurers and gossipers, putting forth no work and no effort to study and improve. To them it is a social club, a place to hang out with the homeboys, drink a little wine, then go home and play dominoes. The vessels of dishonor are here to try you, and every bird clings to its like; see who groups together.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: you have to know your circle. When the Bishop came into the truth he had a circle of five or six brothers he was always getting in trouble around, down to jumping the turnstile with them and getting a ticket. He had to change his circle and get around leadership and the elders to get his mind right. Don’t worry about hurting feelings; if you know they are not right, separate from them.

“he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” Then God can use you. Then we can send that brother to a city or a state and he can grow a whole congregation, like Isaiah telling the Lord, send me.

And this is why we cannot join with the other camps: it is based on what we just read. Only a fool would do that. The same purging God does in Isaiah, we must do ourselves.

precepts.text: But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour. The great house is the nation of Israel, and every school. Sanctuary leaders, you must be able to discern the gold brothers and sisters, the silver, the wood, and the earth. If you have no discernment, you will put people in positions that do not fit them, like Marcus Garvey putting friends over his ships who did not know how to run them, and he lost it all. Shake the friendship appointments; ask who is best qualified. Some brothers and sisters are just slow and need time to grow; fine, then do not put them in that position yet. And purge yourself from the wood and earth spirits that treat this truth like a social club instead of the mustard seed of a government, so you can be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use.
precepts.point: And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. And he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey: when you repent and come to this truth, everybody around you starts hating you. And the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is the nation of Israel; think of it as whatever IUIC school you come from. Every camp leader, the head of the sanctuary, must be able to identify the gold brothers and the silver brothers, the gold sisters and silver sisters, and also look through the school and say, this brother and this sister is earth, this one is wood.

If you can't discern that, you'll have problems in the school, putting people in positions that don't fit them. Marcus Garvey had his ships and put his best friends over them, and they didn't know how to run a ship: one crashed, one went to his girlfriend's house, and he lost it all because of friendship. Shake the friendship appointments. Who is best qualified? Who knows what they're doing? A dummy who doesn't study set up as a school leader, and all hell breaks loose. If sanctuary leaders have no discernment, they are spiritually blind and destined for ruin.

Some brothers and sisters are just slow and need more time to grow. Fine; don't put them in that position yet if others are better qualified. “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work.” Purge yourself from the wood and earth spirits. They see this truth not as a government, not as the mustard seed of a government, but as a social club, dancing every new moon and confused when it comes to God's work. That is how a people groping like the blind becomes vessels unto honour.

precepts.text: If a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully. You want to be an officer, a captain, a deacon; you are not crowned except you strive lawfully. Story told in class: a brother who kept failing the officer of 50 test got a copy of the answers and disseminated it. You might think it is just cheating. No: officers of 50 counsel people. Now a brother who could not pass it is counseling marriages, and he is not qualified for that rank yet. Counsel must be accurate, on point, and scriptural, not from your heart.
precepts.point: For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God. Sometimes we take the laws of the Most High for granted with the mentality, I can sin and God won't do nothing.
precepts.why:
Jason undermined his own brother to become high priest. All of this ties into us today. “And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.” You want to be an officer, a captain, a deacon, a bishop; you want to be moved up. You are not crowned except you strive lawfully.

Just as Jason undermined his brother, we have had brothers in here do the same thing. A brother said, we keep failing the officer of 50 test; I’ll get a copy with the answers and disseminate it. You might think, oh, it’s just cheating. No. It is worse than that. The officers of 50 counsel people. Now you have a brother who couldn’t pass it, who cheated and became an officer of 50, and he is counseling marriages. Y’all don’t see nothing wrong with that?

He is not qualified for that rank yet. The captains and deacons spend time on the exam, with variations on it, to see each man’s level of understanding, and a lot of it is counseling questions. The counselors mostly come from married men, and counsel must be accurate, on point and scriptural, not from your heart.

That is striving unlawfully, the same as Jason buying the priesthood. And a man who strives that way is not crowned.

precepts.text: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth; but shun profane and vain babblings. He embarrassed himself and his organization, and nobody junior to him corrected him. Here, if a captain says something crazy, a captain junior to him corrects him, because there are checks and balances.
precepts.point: You cannot boast in sacrificing as though it makes you special, because it is done; Christ died for us. Justification is through Christ, and it is in the same chapter as let God be true and every man a liar.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
This is one of the first scriptures we learned when we came into this truth, elementary but important: “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” An elder has men under him who look to him for wisdom, knowledge and understanding. The brother who said a man’s deeds are what his son did today embarrassed the hell out of himself and his organization. Now he is being clowned, and because he represents the Israelite community, they label us all as stupid. And never trust a man wearing dark sunglasses inside: he can hide his embarrassment and his eyes. Brother, you have to repent and change your ways.

“But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.” That is profane and vain babbling; it doesn’t make any sense. And nobody in the room, nobody equal to his rank, says, hey, listen, brother, next time. He keeps having a pattern of doing the same thing.

Here, if a captain starts talking crazy, a captain junior to him is going to correct him, because we represent Israel United in Christ, and our elders have taught us with knowledge, wisdom and understanding how to conduct ourselves. There are checks and balances. That brother does not have any of that, and so he cannot rightly divide Romans 3.

precepts.text: No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life, that he may please him who chose him to be a soldier. Christ chose us; when Ezekiel saw the exceeding great army he saw purple and gold, because who else is going nation to nation and island to island teaching?
precepts.point: We look not at the things which are seen, which are temporal, but at the things not seen, which are eternal. America influences the whole world in music and culture, but this power will fall; the kingdom we cannot see yet lasts forever. Stack your bricks and do not be a situational Israelite.
precepts.why:
“for the things which are seen are temporal”: the things we see now are temporary. They are not going to last forever, so there is no need for us to get caught up in the things of the world. The United States of America is the world superpower and influences the whole world. Whatever music is played in America, whatever is in pop culture, the whole world responds to it. But this regime, this power, will fall, thus saith the Lord. Now we have to put our focus on overcoming the beast.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”. Anybody in this war against evil does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life, “that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” Who chose us? Our Lord and Saviour, Jesus the Christ. He chose us to be soldiers in his military.

When Ezekiel saw that exceeding great army, he saw purple and gold. Who else is out there as foot soldiers, going nation to nation, island to island, land to land, teaching the word of God? It is not to boast; it is just the reality.

So a soldier keeps his eyes on what is not seen. We do not see the kingdom right now, but the Lord lets us know it will last forever. The Lord is doing his job; it is time for us to do ours.

precepts.text: The Lord knoweth them that are his, and he establishes leaders to guide you past the wiles of Satan. In a great house, Israel, there are vessels of gold and silver and also of wood and earth, some to honour and some to dishonour. Purge yourself from the wood and earth, the dead spirits always in some mess who separate from leadership and sit with the clique in the back, and you will be a vessel unto honour, meet for the master's use. You learned what the new moon was from a leadership video and now you avoid them?
precepts.point: The fear is not the fear of the servant who hid his talent or the brother making excuses because he is nervous; Psalms 119:120, my flesh trembleth for fear of thee and I am afraid of thy judgments. He is the King of terrors.
precepts.why:
“Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his.” The Lord already knows who are his; we do not, but God does. And God also establishes leaders to guide you along the way, so that you do not fall into the wiles of Satan or stumble into pitfalls and never recover.

“And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” That is purging from sin, from the spiritual leaven, the same as “by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.”

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is Israel. Just as not all the crops take root, in the house of Israel you have the good ones and the bad ones, some to honour and some to dishonour.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: not from the gold and silver, but from the wood and the earth. Those who are not producing fruit, those with dead spirits, those always caught up in some mess, those who separate from the leaders the Lord established. How did you learn what the new moon was? You saw a video of our leadership teaching it. But then you come in here and do not want to be around them; you want to be with the clique in the back. That is the wood and the earth, and God is telling you to purge yourself from those people if you want to remain steadfast in Christ.

Then “he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” God can use you.

precepts.text: Endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
precepts.point: Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war and my fingers to fight. He handpicked every Israelite to be a soldier.
precepts.why:
“Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.” We serve a God of war, the God that formed the light and created darkness, and that God of war is Christ. David is speaking of how the Lord equipped him with his mighty fighting skills, and the same man of war teaches his soldiers to do the same. Paul says it: “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.”

The God of war handpicked every one of us to be soldiers in his mighty army. We are in a boot camp, a training camp, and he is teaching us how to war. Some brothers think they are here just for the unleavened bread, just to be around the brothers. No. Everything going on in the earth, in your household and in the congregation is a teachable moment, because there are spirits in all of it, and we are being built up to deal with those spirits.

It is a process. You start with yourself, subduing your own body, and that is ongoing until you go in the grave. Then your household, then the congregation, as a leader helping other brothers and sisters do the same. Even when you hear somebody else being corrected, it is about you, because at some point you will stand in that same position.

Judges shows why the nations are here: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them”, “to teach them war.” The nations are the Lord's sword to teach us war. If you think that means go get your Glock, you are being simple. “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh.” At Ai the Lord said, “I have given into thy hand the king of Ai”, and still told Joshua, “lay thee an ambush for the city behind it.” The victory is already ordained, but you must go about it the way the Lord commanded. The spiritual side of the war is obedience.

So endure hardness. Some send emails saying, I am no longer with IUIC, I am going to take a break. Taking a break from the Lord? That will not work. A good soldier does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life; he stays in the fight to please the one who chose him.

precepts.text: The Lord knoweth them that are his. Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity; in a great house are vessels to honour and to dishonour.
precepts.point: Examine yourselves whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves, except ye be reprobates. Everyone knows the demons they fight in secret.
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” No one can examine you; you examine yourself. “Know ye not your own selves”: you know the evil you are fighting inside, the thoughts you have, the things you do in secret thinking no one sees you. Look in the mirror and ask, self, am I real? Some say they are in the faith, but in secret they are in the midst of all type of evil, giving in again and again to lasciviousness and fornication. If you cannot examine yourself, you are reprobate. Paul prayed “that ye do no evil”, and the same goes for brothers and sisters today.

Then Timothy: “Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his.” God knows who belongs to him. “And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” Every one of us that calls upon the name of the Lord must depart from iniquity. You brothers should not be adulterers, dealing with prostitutes, dealing with hoes. You sisters should not be sleeping around. No one should be doing schemes and credit card fraud.

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” There are not just vessels of gold here in IUIC. The dishonourable one is faking it in here, here for his own reasons and ulterior motives. So ask yourself: am I real or am I fake? Which vessel are you? Only you alone know, and you have to choose which one you want to be.

Every one of us has demons and thorns we are fighting, so do not act perfect here while Satan has you in a chokehold during the week. We understand you are burning after years of doing it on the regular and now going cold turkey, but come talk to the brothers, go talk to the sisters, and ask for help. Do not let your sins weigh you down and destroy you, because God will judge.

precepts.text: In a great house there are vessels of gold, silver, wood, and earth; that house is the house of Israel.
precepts.point: The waters that issue out from under the threshold are the word of the Most High. Just as a tub fills when the water is left running, the word is now being issued out to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Ezekiel 47: The Waters Issuing from the House

precepts.why:
